title: Boundary normalization with shared single-complex witnesses
statement: Let C be an abelian category with its chosen derived category, and let q:X→X′ and r:Y→Y′ be two morphisms of C. For arbitrary supplied arrows a and beta, define singleBoundaryEquality(q,r,a,beta) to be finiteBoundaryEquality of [def-sp-tower-class-finite] with quotient single(q) in degree zero and root map single(r)[2]. Thus it asserts the existence of arrows a′:single(X′)→single(Y′)[2] and beta′:single(X)→single(Y)[2] heterogeneously equal to a and beta, respectively, such that single(q)≫a′=beta′≫single(r)[2]. All four objects and both fixed morphisms are retained; no condition is added or removed.

source.place: Classes clauses (2)--(3), finite Kummer boundary and supported finite normalization.

proof.text: Apply DerivedCategory.singleFunctor C 0 to q and r, shift the latter by two, and pass these two maps and the supplied arrows to finiteBoundaryEquality. Performing this construction for arbitrary C shares the chosen derived-category and category witnesses before specializing the large coefficient sheaves. Unfolding gives the original finite supported normalization expression exactly. This also applies to zero objects and identity or zero morphisms; the predicate imposes precisely the same equation.
